userPresets.emptyHint: Import parameters from your own literature or measurements.
userPresets.modalSub: Enter biophysical parameters from your experimental measurements or literature source. A parameter source citation is required for all profiles.
userPresets.roleTargetSub: Cancer, bacteria, virus: the cell you are targeting
userPresets.roleHealthySub: Healthy or control cell, used for selectivity comparison
userPresets.fieldSourceSub: Required: literature citation, DOI, or measurement method used to obtain the parameters above
userPresets.radiusBinWarn: Radius was outside the typical range for {type}; it was replaced with the type default. Previous value: {prev} µm → {forced} µm.
userPresets.sigmaProvSectionSub: σ_i is the most uncertain Schwan parameter. Recording the measurement technique and ±% band lets the digital twin weight this preset accurately against others in the community library.
userPresets.fieldSigmaSourceSub: How σ_i was determined. More specific sources carry higher weight in community priors.
userPresets.fieldSigmaCitationSub: DOI, author-year, or measurement protocol identifier for the σ_i value specifically (if distinct from the overall Parameter Source).
userPresets.sigmaCitationPlaceholder: e.g. Gascoyne & Vykoukal (2002) J Phys D 35:R83
userPresets.tipSigmaUncertaintyPct: σ_i Uncertainty ±% The ±% band around the entered intracellular conductivity. Represents how tightly this value is known given the measurement technique. Typical: literature 20-45% · electrorotation 8-15% · impedance spectroscopy 10-20% · dielectrophoretic crossover 15-25%. The simulator uses this band to weight σ_i-dependent outputs (τ, fc, SAR) and to propagate uncertainty when aggregating into the community library.
userPresets.tipSigmaSource: σ_i Measurement Source How the intracellular conductivity was obtained. Literature: value taken from a published source. Measured: measured in your own lab but technique not specified. Electrorotation fit: σ_i obtained from electrorotation spectrum fitting (high specificity). Impedance spectroscopy: σ_i obtained from broadband impedance fit. Estimated: extrapolated or adapted from a similar cell type. More specific sources carry higher weight in the community σ_i prior.
userPresets.tipSigmaCitation: σ_i Citation / Protocol Citation or protocol identifier for the σ_i value specifically. Use when the σ_i source differs from the overall Parameter Source (e.g. morphology and thresholds from paper A, σ_i from your own electrorotation measurement). Leave blank if the overall Parameter Source already covers σ_i.
userPresets.nuclearSectionSub: Optional. Enables Kotnik & Miklavcic (2006) double-shell model for nuclear Vm and NE-selective disruption.
userPresets.fieldNuclearEpsSub: Effective ε_r; lipid bilayer 2-5, NPC raises to 5-12
userPresets.fieldNucleoplasmSigmaSub: S/m, typically slightly higher than cytoplasm
userPresets.fieldNuclearVmThrSub: V, Vm_nuc required for nuclear envelope disruption
userPresets.fieldCapsidQMinSub: Lower limit of Lorentzian Q band
userPresets.fieldCapsidQMaxSub: Upper limit of Lorentzian Q band
userPresets.fieldResFreq2Sub: GHz, leave blank for single-mode resonators
userPresets.fieldCapsidQ2Sub: Defaults to primary Q if blank
userPresets.fieldResMode2AmpSub: 0-1, relative DR contribution of the 2nd mode

userPresets.sourceRequired: Parameter source is required. Enter a literature citation (e.g. author, year, journal) or measurement method (e.g. electrorotation, patch-clamp).
userPresets.tipRadius: Cell Radius R [µm] Dominant size parameter in the Schwan equation. Vm proportional to R: larger cells charge to higher transmembrane voltages at the same field. Also sets the characteristic frequency: fc = 1/(2pi x tau), tau proportional to R. How to measure: flow cytometry (Coulter pulse width), confocal microscopy, AFM. Typical ranges: mammalian 5-20 µm · bacteria 0.5-2 µm · virus 0.02-0.15 µm Ref: Gabriel et al. (1996); Gascoyne & Vykoukal (2002).
userPresets.tipMemThick: Membrane Thickness d [nm] Sets membrane capacitance: Cm = epsilon_r x epsilon_0 / d Thicker membrane means lower Cm, higher fc, and greater field tolerance. How to obtain: standard value 7-9 nm for lipid bilayer (TEM, X-ray diffraction). For bacteria, use the equivalent electrical thickness (not the physical wall thickness); gram-negative bilayer ~7 nm, peptidoglycan layer is resistive not capacitive. Typical: mammalian 5-10 nm · bacteria (bilayer equivalent) 5-10 nm · virus envelope 3-8 nm Ref: Kotnik & Miklavcic (2000) Biophys J 79:670.
userPresets.tipEpsR: Membrane Permittivity epsilon_r Effective dielectric constant of the lipid bilayer. Physical bilayer epsilon_r approximately 2-5; NPC channels and proteins raise the effective value to 5-15 for mammalian cells. Higher epsilon_r means higher Cm, lower fc, and lower lysis field at DC. How to obtain: electrorotation crossover frequency, or take from published Schwan fits for the cell type. Ref: Kotnik & Miklavcic (2000); Foster & Schwan (1989).
userPresets.tipSigmaI: Intracellular Conductivity sigma_i [S/m] Cytoplasm ionic conductivity. Affects both tau (via RC formula) and alpha (internal field factor for SAR). This is the most uncertain Schwan parameter: literature range spans 0.2-1.2 S/m depending on measurement technique, osmolarity, and growth phase. How to obtain: impedance spectroscopy, dielectrophoretic crossover fitting (Gascoyne method), or electrorotation. Patch-clamp gives membrane not cytoplasm sigma. Typical: mammalian cytoplasm 0.4-1.5 S/m · gram-negative bacteria 0.2-0.5 S/m · gram-positive 0.15-0.4 S/m · virus interior 0.05-0.4 S/m (protein-dense interiors can be much lower). Ref: Gascoyne & Vykoukal (2002); Schwan (1957).
userPresets.tipVmThr: Lysis Threshold Vm [V] Pulse-regime caveat (read before entering): This threshold is pulse-width dependent. The commonly cited 200-500 mV range (Weaver & Chizmadzhev 1996) applies to µs-scale IRE pulses where the membrane is fully charged (tp much greater than tau). For ns-scale pulses, the effective threshold rises by the inverse of the pulse-envelope factor: Vm_eff = Vm_thr / (1 - exp(-tp/tau)), which can be 3-14x higher. Enter the threshold for µs-scale IRE conditions; the model applies the pulse-envelope correction automatically for shorter pulses via the Pulse Width slider. How to obtain: patch-clamp + threshold titration, or take from published IRE experiments on the cell type at µs pulse widths. Typical (µs IRE): mammalian 0.5-1.5 V · bacteria 0.8-2 V · virus (envelope disruption) 0.3-0.8 V Ref: Weaver & Chizmadzhev (1996); Teissie & Rols (1993).
userPresets.tipDensity: Cell Density rho [kg/m³] Used in SAR = sigma_i x alpha² x E² x wf / rho. For most mammalian cells, density is approximately 1000-1100 kg/m³ (close to water: 1000 kg/m³). Variation within mammalian cell types is small and has a weak effect on SAR relative to sigma_i uncertainty. Bacteria: ~1050-1150 kg/m³ (higher dry mass fraction). Viruses: ~1100-1400 kg/m³ (highly variable by genome/capsid composition). If no specific measurement is available, use the type default.
userPresets.tipCp: Specific Heat Capacity cp [J/(kg·K)] Used in temperature calculation: T_ss = 37 + SAR x dc / (lambda x cp). Mammalian cells: ~3000-4000 J/(kg·K) (dominated by intracellular water). Variation between cell types is small. Bacteria: ~3000-4000 J/(kg·K). Dry virus particle: ~1000-2000 J/(kg·K) (rarely the limiting factor in vitro). If no specific measurement is available, use the type default. This parameter has a much smaller effect on selectivity than radius or sigma_i.
userPresets.tipDerivedFc: Corner Frequency fc [kHz] Computed from your entered parameters and the current medium conductivity. fc = 1/(2pi x tau) tau = R x Cm x (2 x sigma_e + sigma_i) / (2 x sigma_e x sigma_i) Below fc: Vm is at its Schwan maximum. Above fc: Vm falls as 1/f. This is the key frequency to operate below for maximum disruption. The fc shown updates live as you change parameters.
userPresets.tipCellType: Cell Type Sets the physics mode used for targeting. Mammalian: Schwan transmembrane voltage model (IRE / selectivity mode). Bacteria: Schwan model + optional acoustic cell-wall resonance (GHz range). Virus: Acoustic capsid resonance model (GHz range) + Schwan approximation. Cell category is also auto-detected from radius: R less than 0.1 µm means virus, R less than 2 µm means bacteria.
userPresets.tipResFreq: Resonant Frequency f_res [GHz] Fundamental acoustic resonant frequency of the capsid or cell wall. For rigid-shell model: f_res approximately v_sound / (2R), using capsid speed of sound (~1500-3000 m/s). E. coli ~10-25 GHz · MRSA ~40-60 GHz · Influenza ~0.7 GHz · SARS-CoV-2 ~0.6 GHz. In practice these frequencies require rectangular waveguide or resonant cavity hardware.
userPresets.tipCapsidQ: Quality Factor Q Controls the sharpness of the resonance peak: bandwidth = f_res / Q. Higher Q means more frequency-selective disruption but tighter targeting bandwidth. Bacteria: Q approximately 3-5 (viscoelastic peptidoglycan wall damps resonance). Virus: Q approximately 6-12 (rigid capsid protein shell).
userPresets.tipResThr: Resonance Threshold [V/cm] Field amplitude at the resonant frequency required to achieve disruption. High-Q capsids need less field at resonance; low-Q bacteria need more. Estimate from literature acoustic disruption experiments. Typical range 500-15000 V/cm.
userPresets.tipSigmaMem: Membrane Conductivity σ_mem [S/m] Small through-membrane conductance used in the Clausius-Mossotti factor K(ω) for dielectrophoresis (DEP). Mammalian lipid bilayer: approximately 10⁻⁷ S/m (default if blank). Gram-negative bacteria (porins): approximately 10⁻⁵ S/m. How to obtain: electrorotation fits, impedance spectroscopy. Effect on Schwan Vm is second-order; the main effect is on the DEP crossover frequency f_cross. Ref: Markx & Davey (1999); Arnold & Zimmermann (1988).
userPresets.tipNuclearRadius: Nuclear Radius R_nuc [µm] Nucleus radius; typically ~50% of cell radius for most mammalian cell types. Sets the nuclear Vm bandpass peak frequency (usually 0.7-2 MHz). Ref: Kotnik & Miklavcic (2006) Biophys J 90:480.
userPresets.tipNuclearMemThick: Nuclear Envelope Thickness d_ne [nm] Effective double-membrane thickness. The nuclear envelope is a double bilayer (inner + outer nuclear membrane) with a perinuclear lumen; effective electrical thickness is ~15-40 nm. Ref: Kotnik & Miklavcic (2006).
userPresets.tipNuclearEps: Nuclear Envelope Permittivity ε_ne Effective dielectric constant of the nuclear envelope. Pure lipid bilayer: ~2-5. Nuclear pore complexes (NPC) raise the effective value to ~5-12 due to aqueous channels. Ref: Kotnik & Miklavcic (2006).
userPresets.tipNucleoplasmSigma: Nucleoplasm Conductivity σ_nuc [S/m] Ionic conductivity of the nucleoplasm. Typically slightly higher than cytoplasm (more free ions, less organelle crowding). Typical range: 1.0-1.8 S/m. Ref: Kotnik & Miklavcic (2006).
userPresets.tipNuclearVmThr: Nuclear Envelope Lysis Threshold [V] Minimum Vm across the nuclear envelope required for NE disruption. Typically lower than the plasma membrane threshold; literature range 0.2-1.0 V. NE disruption can cause targeted cell death even when the plasma membrane is intact. Ref: Beebe et al. (2003); Kotnik & Miklavcic (2006).
userPresets.tipResFreqUnc: f_res Uncertainty ±% band The resonant frequency depends on capsid speed of sound which has a literature range. Bacteria v_wall ≈ 800-1200 m/s → ±25-30%. Enveloped viruses v_eff poorly defined → ±40%. The chart shows a Lorentzian envelope across this uncertainty range so you can tune f experimentally.
userPresets.tipCapsidQMin: Q lower bound Lower limit of the Lorentzian resonance Q band. Lower Q gives a broader but weaker resonance peak. Dykeman & Sankey (2010) validated Q on rigid icosahedral capsids; soft walls (bacterial peptidoglycan, viral lipid envelopes) have lower Q values.
userPresets.tipCapsidQMax: Q upper bound Upper limit of the Lorentzian resonance Q band. Higher Q gives a sharper, taller peak. Bacteria 3-5 · enveloped virus 6-10 · rigid icosahedral capsid 10-20.
userPresets.tipResFreq2: Second Mode f_res [GHz] (optional) Some capsids have multiple acoustic modes. Example: SARS-CoV-2 dipolar mode 1 at ~4 GHz, mode 2 at ~7.5 GHz. Leave blank for single-mode resonators. Ref: Yang et al. (2015); Babincova et al. (2000).
userPresets.tipCapsidQ2: Second Mode Q (optional) Quality factor of the second resonance mode. Defaults to the primary Q if left blank. Higher-order modes typically have similar or slightly lower Q than the fundamental.
userPresets.tipResMode2Amp: Second Mode Amplitude [0-1] Relative contribution of the second mode to the disruption ratio. Total DR = DR_mode1 + amp2 × DR_mode2. Typical: 0.3-0.7. Set to 0 to disable the second mode without removing its parameters.
